segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Right.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Are we all here?

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: OK.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: As you know, today Vivien is going to do a presentation on the hat-making project she did with her class during her last teaching practice.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: So, over to you, Vivien.

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: Thanks.

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: Um . . .

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: Mr Yardley has asked me to describe to you the project I did as a student teacher at a secondary school in London.

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: I was at this school for six weeks and I taught a variety of subjects to a class of fourteen-year-old pupils.

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: The project I chose to do was a hat-making project and T think this project could easily be adapted to suit any age.

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: So, to explain the project.. .

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: After we’d done the research, we went back to the classroom to make two basic hat shapes using rolls of old wallpaper.

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: We each made, first of all, a conical hat by ... er ... if I show you now . . . cutting out a circle and then making one cut up to the centre and then ... er ... overlapping the cut like this this ... a conical hat that sits on your head.

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: The other hat we made was a little more complicated ... er ... first of all we cut out a circle again . . . like this . . . then you need a long piece with flaps on it - I’ve already made that bit which I Tipescripts have here - you bend the flaps over and stick them . .. with glue or prittstick . . . to the underside of the circle . .. like this.

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: Again, I’ve prepared this so that I don’t get glue everywhere.

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: The pupils do, of course, so you need plenty of covers for the table.

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: And there you have a pillbox hat as in pill and box.

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: Now variations and combinations of these two hat shapes formed the basis of the pupils’ final designs. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ The next stage of the project was the design phase and this involved, first of all, using their pages of research to draw a design of their hat on paper.

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: That’s the easy part.

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: They then had to translate their two-dimensional design into a form to fit their head.

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: I encouraged them to make a small-scale, three-dimensional hat first so that they could experiment with how to achieve the form they required and I imposed certain constraints on them to keep things simple.

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: For , they had to use paper not card.

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: Paper is more pliable and easier to handle.

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: They also had to limit their colours to white, grey or brown shades of paper which reflected the colours of the buildings they were using as a model for their hats and they had to make sure their glue didn’t show!

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: Well, it was very enjoyable and just to give you an idea of what they produced, I’ve brought along three hats to show you.

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: This one here is based on a circular stairway in an old building in London.

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: It uses three pillbox hats one on top of the other.

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: This was designed by Theresa.

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: Here’s another one that has a simple strip going round the base of the hat but has then gone on to add strips of paper that come out from the base and that meet at the top of the hat -rather like a crown - making a fairly tall hat.

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: This was made by Muriel.

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: And lastly there’s a combination of the pillbox or single strip around the base and then the conical hat shape on top to form a castle turret.

segments.speaker: VIVIEN
segments.en: This was made by Fabrice, and there are many more that I could have brought.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Thank you, Vivien.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: That was most interesting.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Now what we can learn from this is that.. .
